note: Rotation for the daily problem. tools/blog.py next-theme picks the theme used least recently (ties by order). Add a theme by adding an entry; 'reference' is the kit's own notes, 'db_text' the label Problemesis prints (use it to read examples, never to copy). 'stretch' themes are attempted only when the run has time left after a sound simpler version.

themes.name: Black correction
themes.definition: A black piece's random move allows one mate; its corrections stop that mate but commit a new error that allows another.

themes.name: Changed mates
themes.definition: The same black defences are answered by different mates in the set play (or a try) and after the key.

themes.name: Dombrovskis paradox
themes.definition: A try threatens mate A and is refuted by defence a; after the key, the same defence a allows mate A.

themes.name: Flight-giving key
themes.definition: The key gives the black king a new square; the flight is answered by a mate of its own.

themes.name: Self-blocks
themes.definition: Black defences that occupy a square next to their own king, each allowing a different mate.

themes.name: Grimshaw
themes.definition: A black rook and bishop interfere with each other on one square; each interference allows a different mate.

themes.name: Half-pin
themes.definition: Two black units on a line to their king; when one moves, the other is pinned and the mate exploits it.

themes.name: Self-pin
themes.definition: A black defence pins itself against its king, and the mate exploits the pin.

themes.name: Underpromotion key
themes.definition: The key promotes to a minor piece or rook; the other promotions fail for stated reasons.

themes.name: White correction
themes.definition: The key piece's random move fails to one defence; its corrections fix that but fail to another; the key is the correction with no negative effect.

themes.name: Bristol clearance
themes.definition: The key piece travels along a line to clear it for another piece that follows in the threat or the mate.

themes.name: Corner key
themes.definition: The key goes to a corner square, the least natural post on the board, for a precise reason.

themes.name: Novotny
themes.definition: A white piece sacrifices itself on the intersection of two black lines; each capture interferes with the other line.

themes.name: Le Grand
themes.definition: Threat and variation mate swap between a try and the solution for the same pair of defences.

themes.name: Zagoruiko
themes.definition: Two black defences each get different mates in at least three phases.

themes.name: Reciprocal change
themes.definition: Two defences swap their mates between two phases: a A, b B in one; a B, b A in the other.

themes.name: Rudenko
themes.definition: Several tries with double threats; each defence that stops one threat allows the other, and the key shows the cycle.
